title: Prague vs Budapest: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Prague and Budapest based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.summary: This section only exists in the Budapest column — Prague has no thermal bath tradition. categories.title: 🛡️ Safety
categories.summary: Both Prague and Budapest are among Europe's safer cities for tourists. Violent crime affecting visitors is rare in both. The issues are petty theft and scams, and each city has its own flavors.

faqs.question: Is Prague or Budapest cheaper to visit?
faqs.answer: Both are among Europe's most affordable capitals, but Budapest edges it on cost. Expect to spend around €55–75/day mid-range in Budapest versus €60–80/day in Prague. faqs.answer: Budapest wins on nightlife — the ruin bars are genuinely unique experiences you won't find anywhere else in Europe. faqs.question: Are Budapest's thermal baths worth it?
faqs.answer: Absolutely — Budapest's thermal baths are the city's most unique attraction and something Prague cannot offer. faqs.answer: Prague has the edge for sheer medieval density — the Old Town, Charles Bridge, and Prague Castle complex are a concentrated architectural masterpiece. faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Prague or Budapest?
faqs.answer: April–May and September–October for both cities. Avoid July–August: summer crowds are intense and prices spike 30–50%. faqs.answer: Yes — they're 7 hours apart by direct train (Regiojet or ÖBB, around €20–35 one way), 1 hour by budget flight (€30–60), or 8 hours by Flixbus. faqs.answer: Both are among Europe's safer cities for tourists.
